ops.old: The Pennsylvania Rural Health Model demonstrated the payoff directly: globally-budgeted rural hospitals proved more resilient to volume loss during COVID-19, when fee-for-service hospitals saw revenue crater as elective volume vanished but budgeted hospitals kept their fixed income. That natural experiment is the clearest proof that decoupling revenue from volume works exactly as the theory predicts.
ops.new: The Pennsylvania Rural Health Model (2017–2024) illustrated the stability argument during COVID-19: when elective volume vanished, its participating rural hospitals continued to receive their fixed global-budget payments while fee-for-service revenue cratered elsewhere. That is the core of the theory — revenue that does not depend on volume — although the model never grew beyond a small group of hospitals, and stability is not the same as proof that global budgets improve care or reduce cost.
ops.claim: PA Rural Health Model "demonstrated the payoff directly"; "clearest proof" via COVID natural experiment
ops.sources: CMS PA Rural Health Model page (all-payer global budgets 2019-2024; ended 2024-12-31); no evaluation establishing the COVID comparison as proof
ops.note: Overstated evidentiary claim softened to what is documented; model ended.
